Combine perturbation assays created by the mixed-layer workflow

CombinePerturbAssays.Rd

Experimental replacement for CombinePerturbAssays(). This function is designed for perturbation assays in which direct targets (hub genes or user-selected genes) are changed in the counts layer and secondary genes are changed by network propagation in the log-normalized data layer.

Usage

CombinePerturbAssays(
  seurat_obj,
  perturb_assays,
  baseline_assay = "RNA",
  new_assay = paste0(paste(perturb_assays, collapse = "_"), "_combined"),
  scale.factor = 10000,
  direct_tolerance = 0,
  check_provenance = TRUE,
  require_provenance = FALSE,
  strict_provenance_check = TRUE,
  floor_counts = TRUE,
  floor_data = TRUE,
  allow_dense = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

A Seurat object containing the baseline and perturbation assays.

perturb_assays

Character vector naming the perturbation assays.

baseline_assay

Name of the assay from which the perturbations were generated. Default is "RNA".

new_assay

Name for the combined assay.

scale.factor

Scale factor used by the perturbation workflow's log-normalization. Default is 1e4.

direct_tolerance

Non-negative numeric tolerance used to infer direct genes from count-space deltas. A gene is direct for an assay when any cell has abs(perturbed_count - baseline_count) > direct_tolerance.

check_provenance

Logical; inspect assay@misc$COMPACT metadata written by StampPerturbProvenance() and verify that every available stamp names baseline_assay and includes the "counts" layer. Missing stamps warn but do not stop unless require_provenance = TRUE. Default is TRUE.

require_provenance

Logical; require complete provenance metadata for every perturbation assay. Default is FALSE, allowing older or unstamped assays to be combined after a warning.

strict_provenance_check

Logical; stop when an available provenance stamp conflicts with baseline_assay or does not include "counts". If FALSE, issue a warning and continue. Default is TRUE.

floor_counts

Logical; floor negative combined counts at zero. This can be needed when several knock-down deltas affect the same gene. Default is TRUE.

floor_data

Logical; floor negative combined log-expression at zero, matching ApplyPropagation(). Default is TRUE.

allow_dense

Logical; permit dense input matrices. Default is FALSE to protect against accidental memory expansion.

overwrite

Logical; replace an existing assay named new_assay. Default is FALSE.

verbose

Logical; emit progress messages.

Value

The Seurat object with the new combined assay.

Details

Direct and propagated effects are deliberately combined differently:

  1. Count-space deltas are added to the baseline counts.

  2. The combined counts are log-normalized with the baseline library sizes, reproducing the primary/direct component in data space.

  3. For each input assay, its data-space delta is added only for genes that were not directly changed in that assay. These are the secondary effects produced by propagation.

In symbols, for input assay \(i\), baseline counts \(B\), reconstructed baseline log-expression \(L\), perturbed counts \(P_i\), perturbed data \(D_i\), and direct-gene set \(H_i\) inferred from \(P_i-B\): $$C = max(0, B + sum_i(P_i-B))$$ $$E = max(0, logNorm(C; colSums(B)) + sum_i 1[g not in H_i](D_i-L))$$

This component-wise exclusion is important. If a gene is a direct target in one assay but a secondary target in another, its secondary effect from the other assay is retained.

The function is intentionally kept under a new name so the existing CombinePerturbAssays() implementation remains available for comparison.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
object <- CombinePerturbAssays(
  object,
  perturb_assays = c("M6_up", "M2_down"),
  baseline_assay = "RNA",
  new_assay = "M6up_M2down_"
)
} # }
